Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:
- Beige Book signals mixed but softening conditions: modest-to-moderate growth through late February with early COVID-19 impacts already visible—travel/tourism down (Coronavirus negatively impacts travel), manufacturing facing supply-chain strains, and declines in natural resource extraction/energy, while agriculture was little changed and some transportation activity (e.g., Mid-Atlantic ports) showed pockets of resilience.
- These anecdotes corroborate the FOMC’s concern about energy-sector stress and muted inflation and reinforce SLOOS evidence of tighter bank credit supply and weaker loan demand. However, the Beige Book’s still-firm pre-shock baseline and sectoral variability temper the purely negative signal from SLOOS.

Net effect: maintain a negative tone but slightly less severe than the SLOOS-only downgrade.
